title: fix(state): give one actionable answer for state written by a newer release and keep status reads read-only
body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes contradictory repair advice and SQLite sidecar creation when an older OpenClaw build inspects state written by a newer release. Related: #166906 and #166857.

## User Impact

Doctor, Gateway startup, update status, and offline database preflight consistently recommend a compatible newer build or restoration of the backup matching the older build. They preserve the newer database's bytes, mtimes, and SQLite sidecars. No schema, migration, configuration option, CLI option, or dependency changes.

## Why This Change Was Made

Reuse the existing newer-schema classification and artifact-preserving reader. Doctor omits the generic repair tail; fleet preflight stops interpreting an unsupported registry; offline preflight checks the version before integrity. Update status also prepares its Gateway probe's device identity through the diagnostic reader, because the default asynchronous identity lookup opens a shared actor even for existing-only reads.

The explicit-file preflight implementation moves to a focused sibling to keep the owning module within its line cap. Its existing export remains available, and the native wrapper inventory includes the new module.

## Evidence

- Negative controls reproduce all four defects, including WAL/SHM creation through the real Gateway probe. Assertions compare database bytes, nanosecond mtimes, and sidecar sets.
- Touched suites ran three times: Doctor maintenance (46 tests), explicit-file/Gateway preflight (7 tests), and real-probe status artifact preservation (2 tests). The original status suite remains unchanged and passes with its importers.
- All runnable tests in the 69-importer selection and six repository closure guards passed. Status importers and the affected closure/routing guards passed again after the identity-read fix. Existing platform skips remain unchanged.
- `node scripts/check-changed.mjs --base f0258248b3e0a1fc5a09bd4060a2f494c35b42c9` passed, including full core/test typechecks, full core lint, script lint, ratchets, and import-cycle/closure checks.
- Independent P1 review was attempted through Codex, but both attempts returned HTTP 401 and produced no verdict. Maintainer review of this head is still required. Auto-merge is off.

Fresh isolated copies of released `openclaw@2026.9.8` state used shared-state `user_version` 19 → 21 and the unreadable Workshop index mutation; this build supports schema 20. All five real CLI cases passed on the final build, preserving every SQLite-family file hash, nanosecond mtime, and file-set membership. No service or listener remained active.

| Command | Exit | Result |
| --- | ---: | --- |
| `doctor --json` | 2 | Newer-schema guidance; files unchanged |
| `doctor --fix --non-interactive` | 1 | No repair tail; files unchanged |
| `gateway run --bind loopback --auth none` | 78 | No secondary registry-repair advice; files unchanged |
| `update status --json` | 0 | Partial status with compatible-build/backup guidance; no WAL/SHM creation |
| `database preflight <copied-file> --json` | 1 | `incompatible`, `foundVersion: 21`, actionable reason; files unchanged |

Local one-worker wall times: Doctor 212.22 / 112.31 / 94.83 seconds; preflight 9.31 / 6.10 / 6.05 seconds; status artifacts 46.11 / 36.52 / 22.91 seconds. The status artifact suite spent 10.39 / 17.96 / 13.86 seconds in tests; its real SQLite readers and RPC identity boundary are necessary to expose the sidecar mutation that a mocked probe misses. Doctor's existing maintenance/service-custody matrix accounts for its longer runtime. The broad importer/guard run took 1,221.82 seconds including shared runtime preparation; the final status importer/guard run took 183.60 seconds. Hosted CI seconds are pending at the authoring handoff.

Delta: production +169/-125 (net +44, including the preflight relocation); tests/support +198/-5; tooling +2/-0; docs +6/-0.

Pre-existing slow cases were recorded without increasing timeouts or changing assertions: native wrapper provisioning spent 343.76 seconds in tests (including 98.80 seconds for its cold/warm/sparse checkout sequence), and the original-capture Doctor flow took 46.55 seconds while exercising real custody, backup capture, and repeated repair admission. These inherited costs are unchanged; no timeouts, retries, or assertions were altered.
